items.title: RT Nimesh Shah: Bajaj Fin - Strong Q1; Mgmt opted to defer guidance revision to post-2QFY27, though commentary on underlying business trends remained ...
items.description_html:
RT Nimesh Shah
Bajaj Fin - Strong Q1; Mgmt opted to defer guidance revision to post-2QFY27, though commentary on underlying business trends remained unequivocally constructive.

MOSL on Bajaj Fin
Upgrade to Buy, TP Rs 1300
Firing on all cylinders; a new earnings cycle begins
investment thesis is predicated on three structural pillars:
1) credit cycle has turned, which will enable lower credit costs and higher earnings
2) Multiple growth engines (core lending, digital ecosystem, gold loans, new businesses for BAF) are firing simultaneously
3) Duration and magnitude of this new earnings cycle leave room for both earnings upgrades & valuation support
Raise FY27/FY28 EPS estimates by 4%/2% to factor in higher AUM growth & lower credit costs

CLSA on Bajaj Fin
O-P, TP raised to Rs 1300
Proved itself of iron man status in 1QFY27.
PAT beat estimate by 6% driven by a beat on all fronts – NII, PPOP and credit costs.
AUM growth accelerated from 22% YoY in the preceding quarter to 24% YoY in this quarter.
Calculated margins were largely stable as higher cost of funds was passed on to borrowers.
What stole show this quarter was strong asset quality performance.
Despite making overlay provisions, credit costs declined 30bp YoY to 1.5% (core credit costs of 1.3%)
Believe co can comfortably beat its credit cost guidance of 1.45-1.6% for the year
Management’s tone on analyst concall was strong

CITI on Bajaj Fin
Buy, TP raised to Rs 1300
BAF delivered 30bps RoA expansion to 4.7%, with PAT surging 28% YoY/9% QoQ and RoE breaching 20% mark.
Net stress formation remained in check — GS3/GS2 accretion modest at Rs3.3bn.
Prudent macro-overlay of Rs2.96bn enhanced coverage, yielding reported credit cost of 1.54%.
Notably, core credit cost compressed to 1.31% (well below the guided band of 1.45–1.60%).
NIMs held flat (vs guidance of moderation through FY27), while AUM growth accelerated to 24% YoY — secular and broad-based.
Business/Professional Loans were upgraded from Amber to Green.
Mgmt opted to defer guidance revision to post-2QFY27, though commentary on underlying business trends remained unequivocally constructive.

HSBC on Bajaj Fin
Buy, TP Raised to Rs 1270
1QFY27 was underscored by extremely strong quarterly performance across metrics
Increase AUM growth, NIM, and credit cost estimates
EPS estimates are 1-6% higher over FY27-29e
BAF would revisit its guidance across key metrics post 2QFY27 results.
Management is confident of scaling up its business further, while maintaining profitability at current levels
Co is seeing improvement in asset quality trends in personal & business loans both at industry & company levels

Nomura on Bajaj Fin
Buy, TP Rs 1140
1QFY27 net profit beats est
Strong asset quality performance; management will watch for another quarter before any guidance revision
Cost of funds movement well controlled; management expects it to be rangebound with a slight upward bias
Sustained asset quality trends could trigger better growth outcomes, according to management

Bernstein on Bajaj Fin
U-P, TP Rs 840
Reported a strong quarter, with healthy balance sheet growth & sharply improving asset quality driving earnings momentum.
Consolidated AUM grew 24% YoY, led by continued strength in mortgages, urban consumer finance & emerging segments, while NIMs remained broadly stable, supporting 23% YoY NII growth
Key positive was continued moderation in credit costs, which declined to 1.54%, resulting in a 27% YoY increase in EPS.
Asset quality improved across most portfolios, with the consolidated GNPA ratio declining to 0.96%, while RoA remained stable at a healthy 4.7%

Every once in a while, an SME company completely surprises you with its execution.

Monolithish is proving to be one of those rare outliers. 🧵

What makes an SME truly stand out?

Let’s break it down.

To spot an SME outlier, check these boxes:
✅ Unique business model (not just another commoditized business)
✅ Pricing power & strong vendor ecosystem

Monolithish checks every single one.

📈 Revenue: 64% YoY | 16% QoQ
📈 EBITDA: 99% YoY | 15% QoQ
📈 PAT: 134% YoY | 24% QoQ

Despite a minor revenue miss this quarter, FY27 guidance stays intact at ₹250Cr (+85% YoY).

items.title: 🚨 C2C’s auditor has issued a qualified opinion and flagged multiple serious financial and compliance concerns: 1️⃣ Liquidity & Going Concern Ris...
items.description_html:
🚨 C2C’s auditor has issued a qualified opinion and flagged multiple serious financial and compliance concerns:

1️⃣ Liquidity & Going Concern Risk:
The company is facing a liquidity crisis, with statutory dues unpaid due to lack of funds. Recovery from trade receivables remains uncertain, while operations are heavily dependent on short-term promoter funding. The auditor has raised doubt over C2C’s ability to continue as a going concern. Liquidation Risk

2️⃣ CSR Payments Not Cleared:
CSR expenses were recognised through cheques, creating a book overdraft. However, the cheques were not presented for payment. The auditor noted that the CSR obligation is discharged only when the payment is actually cleared.

3️⃣ Statutory Dues Pending:
Undisputed statutory payments remain unpaid. No provision has been made for possible interest or penalties. Delays in filing statutory returns and weak internal controls were also highlighted.

4️⃣ Labour Code Impact Not Assessed:
The company has not quantified the potential impact of new labour regulations on gratuity, provident fund, wages and other employee benefits.

5️⃣ FEMA Compliance Issues:
Overseas receivables remain unrealised beyond RBI timelines. Applications for regularisation are pending, SOFTEX registration is yet to be approved, and possible penalties have not been provided for.

items.title: Creative Newtech has done an interesting acquisition, transforming from a distributor to a manufacturer of an integrated surveillance technology platf...
items.description_html:
Creative Newtech has done an interesting acquisition, transforming from a distributor to a manufacturer of an integrated surveillance technology platform.

Creative Newtech has approved the acquisition of 100% of Infinova (India) for up to US$4 million, marking a strategic shift beyond distribution into surveillance technology manufacturing.

The acquisition brings Infinova's India operations, brand rights, technical expertise, experienced workforce, and local assembly & manufacturing facility, providing Creative Newtech with immediate execution capabilities.

More importantly, the deal lays the foundation for a 'Make in India' surveillance platform, enabling the company to build proprietary products, strengthen after-sales support, and reduce dependence on third-party distribution.

The transaction also accelerates Creative's transition from a distribution-led business to an integrated, technology-led surveillance solutions provider, giving it greater control over manufacturing, product ownership, and margins.

The company holds all the relevant licenses from Gem, BIS, and STQC, enabling it to access the government portal. STQC shifts 22% market share from Chinese to Indian brands

This is more than an acquisition—it is a business model transformation, positioning Creative Newtech to move up the value chain from distributing surveillance products to designing, assembling, and manufacturing them under a 'Make in India' strategy.

Creative NewTech trades at 18 PE vs Prizor Vtech 42PE vs Aditya Infotech 110PE

A unique re-rating candidate driven by undervaluation, business transformation, and sector tailwinds

items.description_html:
GNG Electronics - Steady Q1FY27

REV increased 32% YoY to 412.5 Cr
PAT increased 56% YoY to 28.9 Cr
EBITDA margin improved to 12.8% vs 11.3% YoY

Management revised its FY27 growth guidance from 25% earlier to 30%

PAT margin guidance was also revised upward by 50-75 bps to around 1% improvement

The biggest theme is the structural shift towards premium refurbished computing

Management highlighted that buyers are no longer only asking whether the device is new

They are asking whether it works well, whether it can be trusted and whether it creates value

This shift is helping Electronics Bazar as new laptop prices continue to rise & affordability becomes a bigger issue

Memory prices increased another 5-10% in Q1FY27

Management said memory prices have gone up almost 5x since October 2025

Entry level laptop prices have increased from around 40,000 to 48,000

Management believes the shortage in memory & critical components may not see meaningful relief before end of 2027

This is creating strong tailwinds for premium refurbished devices

However, management clarified that the business is not dependent only on memory price inflation

The larger opportunity is structural - affordable computing, trust, warranty & organized refurbished devices

India has around 1 Bn mobile phone users, but only around 55-60 Mn personal computers

India also has around 300 Mn students, while Africa has around 250 Mn students

GNG now supplies to 49 countries vs 46 countries at FY26 end

Revenue mix in Q1FY27:
India - 36%
Middle East - 12%
US - 24%
Europe - 23%
Others - 5%

Q1FY27 volumes were also healthy, Total volume growth was 18% YoY

Laptop volume stood at 1.08 lakh units
Desktop and others volume stood at 42,000 units

Management said the business is procurement heavy by design

They buy from large corporates, banks & leasing companies when disposal opportunities come

Having large inventory allows them to supply instantly to large B2B & education customers

Management gave an example where an Australian customer bought 3,000 laptops in one shot because GNG had ready inventory

Management said they have been buying ahead of price increases and this has helped gross margins

Procurement prices have remained broadly stable for GNG due to sourcing reach, contracts & value added services offered to vendors

Currently, refurbished laptops are priced around 30% of new laptop prices

Management compared this with used phones & used cars, where refurbished / used products can trade at around 50% of new product prices

They believe as trust improves, pricing can move from 30% towards 35% and eventually higher

Even a move from 30% to 35% of new laptop price can create meaningful margin expansion

This is the biggest structural margin lever

The company wants to become the most trusted global brand in premium refurbished computing

Management avoided comparing itself with Dell or HP, but clearly wants to build Electronics Bazar as a trusted global refurbished computing brand

items.title: India is expected to emerge as the largest wealth creation opportunity across emerging markets More than $7 Tn of wealth is expected to be added by 20...
items.description_html:
India is expected to emerge as the largest wealth creation opportunity across emerging markets

More than $7 Tn of wealth is expected to be added by 2030 in the >US$250K client segment, with India contributing around $2.37 Tn or nearly 35% of the total opportunity

India’s wealth pool is expected to grow at a CAGR of 12% through 2030, while the number of millionaires is expected to increase by more than 55% by 2029

The growth is being driven by 6%+ GDP growth, rising household savings, financialisation of assets, deeper equity participation & the increasing formalisation of the economy

Wealth creation is also expanding beyond metros into Tier 2 & Tier 3 cities, supported by a new generation of entrepreneurs & affluent professionals

Around 70% of financial assets in India are still invested in traditional products such as deposits, insurance & pension products

Only around 15% of Indian wealth is professionally managed compared with approx 75% in developed markets

Comprehensive wealth platforms are likely to benefit more than mono line players, as affluent clients increasingly prefer a single platform offering advisory, lending, investments, estate planning & alternative products

items.description_html:
RT Surenddra verma
Great Punjabi Lala Jagat Narain.
He spent years in prison for opposing both British rule and the Emergency. He built Punjab Kesari into one of Punjab's most widely read newspapers and refused to bow before terror.

He stood up to Bhindranwale despite repeated threats. He was assassinated for his courage. The sacrifices did not end there-his son, Ramesh Chander, was also killed, along with 52 members of the Punjab Kesari family.

The media group lost:
• 2 Editors
• 7 Reporters
• 20 Distribution Agents
• 23 Hawkers
• 2 Workers

Their only "crime" was refusing to surrender to Khalistani intimidation and continuing to print the truth.

Punjab Kesari also raised funds and supported the families of Hindu and Sikh civilians murdered by Khalistani terrorists when the state had largely failed them.

When fear forced distributors to stop carrying the newspaper, KPS Gill ensured copies were distributed through police stations so the voice of truth would not be silenced.

Lala Jagat Narain, the Punjab Kesari family, and KPS Gill remind us that Punjab was saved not only by brave security personnel but also by fearless journalists and ordinary citizens who refused to bow before terror.

Their sacrifice must never be forgotten. 🇮🇳

items.title: RT Reads with Ravi: Umberto Eco, who owned 50,000 books, had this to say about home libraries: “It is foolish to think that you have to read all the ...
items.description_html:
RT Reads with Ravi
Umberto Eco, who owned 50,000 books, had this to say about home libraries:

“It is foolish to think that you have to read all the books you buy, as it is foolish to criticize those who buy more books than they will ever be able to read. It would be like saying that you should use all the cutlery or glasses or screwdrivers or drill bits you bought before buying new ones.

“There are things in life that we need to always have plenty of supplies, even if we will only use a small portion.

“If, for example, we consider books as medicine, we understand that it is good to have many at home rather than a few: when you want to feel better, then you go to the ‘medicine closet’ and choose a book. Not a random one, but the right book for that moment. That’s why you should always have a nutrition choice!

“Those who buy only one book, read only that one and then get rid of it. They simply apply the consumer mentality to books, that is, they consider them a consumer product, a good. Those who love books know that a book is anything but a commodity.”

items.title: RT Sann: His name is Dinesh Thakur. He gave up a safe, high paying job and spent eight years of his life fighting one of the largest drug companies in...
items.description_html:
RT Sann
His name is Dinesh Thakur.

He gave up a safe, high paying job and spent eight years of his life fighting one of the largest drug companies in the country. He did it because he discovered that the medicines millions of people trusted were built on a lie.

He was a chemical engineer who had worked in America and come back to India for a senior role at Ranbaxy, then the biggest generic medicine maker in the country. It was a proud Indian company whose cheap medicines were sold across the world.

Not long after he joined, he was asked to look into the quality of the company's drugs. What he found frightened him.

The company was faking its test results. Medicines were being sold without being properly tested for whether they were safe, or whether they even worked. The data handed to regulators was simply invented.

These were not luxury goods. These were the tablets that sick people swallowed every day, trusting that they would heal them.

Thakur went to his own bosses with what he had found. Nothing changed. So he made a choice that cost him everything. He resigned, and he reported the company to the American drug regulators.

Then began eight long years. He handed over evidence, sat through investigation after investigation, and lived under the shadow of taking on a giant that had every reason to crush him.

In 2013, it ended. Ranbaxy admitted its guilt in an American court, pleaded guilty to seven serious crimes, and was made to pay one of the largest fines ever handed to a generic drug maker, five hundred million dollars.

Because one man refused to look away, the way the world checks the safety of its medicines was changed for good.

He had a comfortable life and a good salary. He gave it all up so that the medicine in a stranger's hand could be trusted.

items.title: RT The Seeker: It's a shame no major film has been made about Biju Patnaik. He lived a life that sounds almost fictional: In 1938, he flew his entire ...
items.description_html:
RT The Seeker
It's a shame no major film has been made about Biju Patnaik. He lived a life that sounds almost fictional:

In 1938, he flew his entire wedding procession by aircraft to Rawalpindi for his marriage to Gyanwati Sethi (who became the first Indian woman to hold a commercial pilot’s license, and the couple later flew daring missions together.)

While serving in the Royal Indian Air Force (including as head of Air Transport Command), he secretly ferried freedom fighters like Jayaprakash Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia, and Aruna Asaf Ali to their hideouts. He also airdropped 'Quit India' leaflets to Indian troops while evacuating British families.

The British once jailed him for transporting nationalist leaders and distributing anti-British literature but also honored him for bravery in evacuating civilians from Japanese-occupied Burma.

During WWII, he flew daring missions delivering arms and supplies to Soviet forces in Stalingrad, and over the treacherous 'Hump' route to China in
support of Chinese Nationalist forces against the Japanese.

In July 1947, he and his wife flew a Dakota into Indonesia, landed on an improvised airstrip while evading Dutch anti-aircraft fire, rescued Prime Minister Sutan Sjahrir, refuelled using abandoned Japanese fuel, and flew him safely to India via Singapore.

A couple of months later, during the Pakistani invasion of Kashmir, he airlifted one of the first Indian troops into Srinagar.

The same year he founded Kalinga Airlines, one of India's earliest private airlines.

As Odisha CM post-1962 India-China war, he secretly visited CIA headquarters at Langley to forge a covert India-US partnership against China, which led to the Aviation Research Centre (ARC) at Charbatia, which supported U-2 recon missions over Tibet.

He was also a legendary administrator and statesman, laying much of the foundation of Odisha's industrial empire (mines, ports, heavy industries etc).

When he passed away, Indonesia observed 7 days of state mourning. Russia observed 1 day. He remains the only person in Indian history whose body was draped in the national flags of 3 nations - India, Indonesia, and Russia.

Few public figures have left such a footprint.

His extraordinary life needs to be brought to the big screen.


Shiv Aroor: What event in Indian history/recent current affairs do you want to see a film made on?

items.description_html:
Deepak Fertilisers & Petrochemicals Corp: Guidance - -Concall Update

• Management expects Q2 FY27 to see a typical slowdown in mining activities due to monsoon, offset by a pickup in the Crop Nutrition business.

• Both the Gopalpur TAN project (96% complete) and Dahej Nitric Acid project (93% complete) are on track to commence operations in Q2 FY27, with good utilization expected from Q4 FY27, potentially reaching around 80%.

• The company anticipates that the full benefits of Equinor LNG supplies will be realized over the next few quarters as existing contracts phase out, leading to a higher proportion of Equinor gas.

• Net debt is nearing its peak, and deleveraging is expected to begin from FY27 onward as new CapEx projects contribute to EBITDA and cash flow.

• Management expects an elevated new normal by the end of FY27, driven by new CapEx contributions and full benefits from gas supply, leading to a higher base level.

• The company expects its Ras Al Khaimah (UAE) capacity to double and be upstream by Q3 FY26-27.

• For FY26-27, management maintains its guidance of 40 million tonnes for Indian operations, with Q2 volumes projected at 9-9.4 million tonnes, leading to 19.5-20 million tonnes by HY1.

• Fuel costs have almost peaked in Q1, with Q2 expected to stabilize or decrease, assuming no further Middle East disruptions.

• The company aims to revert to a 70% trade and 30% non-trade sales mix, having been forced to increase non-trade sales in Q1 due to coal quality issues.

items.description_html:
Not one partner. Not a handful. One in five.

A Fifth of Nvidia's China Partners Have Sold Into the Blacklist.

India Angle

The centre of gravity in chip policy is shifting from the licensable unit to the reseller, and that reframes India from a passive importer into a jurisdiction whose channel gets audited. Value added resellers and system integrators are the layer under scrutiny here, and India has the same layer standing between global vendors and domestic buyers.

The falsifiable test is whether Indian integrators begin facing formal end user certification, resale restrictions and beneficial ownership disclosure on accelerator sales within the next two procurement cycles.

Volume held flat while documentation load rises would confirm it.

India Built a Phone Export Industry. Now It Needs Customers It Doesn't Have.

India's handset export scheme is aimed at a global market where roughly 61% of units sit outside Apple and Samsung and are served by Chinese brands using Chinese assemblers. The binding constraint is therefore anchor customer access, not incentive quantum or installed capacity, which is why the same policy tool that worked domestically may not repeat offshore.

This is falsified if a non Apple Indian assembler announces a multi year export contract with a top ten global brand.

•Members are ready for a hike: In the first split vote of the Warsh era, three FOMC members would prefer to raise rates in the face of elevated inflation.
•Warsh is trademarking his communication style: The new chair is opposed to forward guidance, preferring that markets and businesses react to real-time financial information.
•FOMC is letting markets take the lead: Warsh wants markets to react to economic shocks and news events in real time, rather than relying on Fed projections.

items.title: Where's FCNR(B) flow gone? @kantisoumya of @TheOfficialSBI says, they are in transit. So far (8 June-17 Jul), FCA up by $7.6 bn, while RBI deposit mob...
items.description_html:
Where's FCNR(B) flow gone? @kantisoumya of @TheOfficialSBI says, they are in transit.
So far (8 June-17 Jul), FCA up by $7.6 bn, while RBI deposit mobilization was $17.4 bn for FCNR(B) flows.
While RBI provides weekly change in FCA every Friday, every bank has a designated time during the week to swap these FCNR(B) deposits with RBI and get equivalent rupee resources. It's possible that FCNR(B) deposit numbers are being captured by RBI and becomes a part of FCA with a lag --with assumption that a large part of foreign exchange reserves is being recouped & adding to RBI's foreign exchange coffers.

Owing to this,  we expect for the next 15 days period (17 Jul-31 Jul) FCA inflows could touch $10-12 billion based on current trends.

It may also be noted that once the swap is done, there will be a corresponding liquidity injection (permanent and temporary) Thus, bank time deposits/ permanent monetary injection have increased by close to Rs 90,000 crores. Core liquidity / Temporary liquidity injection has already at ~Rs 5 lakh crore as of June 30 clearly indicating the impact of FCNR (B) inflows on liquidity.

items.title: Tear gas, lathi charges, pellets, blocking supply of food & water can't do anything to cockroaches They have been around 300+ million years -- predate...
items.description_html:
Tear gas, lathi charges, pellets, blocking supply of food & water can't do anything to cockroaches
They have been around 300+ million years -- predate dinosaurs by 150 million years.
Cockroaches can live for a week without a head.
They can survive a month without food & 2 weeks without water.
They eat anything -- glue, hair, and book bindings.
They can hold their breath for 40 minutes & survive submerged underwater up to 30 minutes.
They have decentralized nervous system. Each of leg-controlling ganglia can operate independently; that’s why a headless roach can still stand & react.
They're incredibly fast; can sprint roughly 50 body lengths per second (like running 200+ mph by a human being).
They can run on 2 legs. At top speed, some cockroaches sprint bipedally, like tiny dinosaurs & move faster.
They can withstand radiation doses many times higher than what's lethal to humans.
They can flatten their bodies and squeeze through gaps as thin as a coin.
A single female can produce hundreds of offspring in a lifetime & they can reproduce without males.
Cockroaches make group decisions democratically. They "vote" on where to shelter. They use collective behaviour to distribute themselves optimally, balancing between staying together and not overcrowding one place.
They can learn and be trained.
They have "personalities." Some are risk-takers who explore exposed areas quickly; others stay cautious and hidden, and these traits stay stable over time.

items.description_html:
Zomato and Swiggy have shown that food delivery can be profitable.

But the largest cloud-kitchen operators, such as Rebel Foods and Curefoods, remain in the red.

Swish believes that combining the two models is the answer: owning the customer interface, the kitchen and the delivery network.

Traditional cloud kitchens and restaurants depend on aggregators for demand, paying commissions and delivery fees that can take away 20–30% of an order’s value.

They bear the cost of running kitchens without controlling customer acquisition, ordering behaviour or repeat usage.

Swish wants to close that gap through its own consumer interface and a 10-minute delivery promise.

It believes this model can generate operating margins of 15–20% on a Rs 250 order.

items.title: India’s app-store market has crossed a $1 billion revenue run rate. In-app purchases on Google Play and Apple’s App Store reached a record $345 mill...
items.description_html:
India’s app-store market has crossed a $1 billion revenue run rate.

In-app purchases on Google Play and Apple’s App Store reached a record $345 million in Q2 2026, according to Sensor Tower.

That is nearly $1.4 billion annualised.

But even at that level, India accounts for less than 1% of global app-store revenue.

For years, global app-store spending was dominated by mobile games. India has never been a major spender on gaming.

That balance is only now shifting globally as non-gaming apps overtook games for the first time in 2025, but still accounted for only slightly more than half of spending.

India presents a more extreme contrast:

- Non-gaming apps now generate about 70% of India’s app-store revenue vs 50-51% globally.

- Non-gaming revenue grew more than 50% YoY to nearly $240 million in Q2 2026, compared with 10% growth in gaming revenue to $106 million.

Entertainment/video apps such as YouTube, Instagram, Crunchyroll and JioHotstar, as well as AI, productivity and utility apps such as Google One, ChatGPT, Claude and LinkedIn, dominate the Indian market in revenues.

Interestingly, Claude’s revenue surged more than 19-fold YoY in Q2, according to Sensor Tower.

items.description_html:
RT Shiv Aroor
Heartbroken & so inspired 💔💔🙏🏽

The Commonwealth Games is becoming a daily roll-call of young Indians who have emerged from unimaginable hardship & horrors to win gold.

Look at 23-year-old judoka Asmita Dey, who is now the first Indian to win Commonwealth Games gold in the women’s 48kg category.

7 months ago, she lost her father to a brain stroke. A bicycle mechanic who earned barely ₹300 a day, he raised his family in a mud house in a small village in Tripura. When a knee injury threatened Asmita’s career, he found the money to take her to Delhi for treatment.

Even as the family mourned, Asmita’s mother urged her daughter to return to training, believing that abandoning the dream would betray everything her father had sacrificed for.

She now stands on top of the Commonwealth Games podium with a gold medal around her neck. https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2083260620657610779/video/1

items.title: RT Peterson Institute: NEW: What's the status of US-China decoupling? How have Trump's tariffs in 2018-19 plus 2025 affected supply chains & US import...
items.description_html:
RT Peterson Institute
NEW: What's the status of US-China decoupling? How have Trump's tariffs in 2018-19 plus 2025 affected supply chains & US imports? @ChadBown explores.
💡Despite the US tariff actions, US real goods imports from the world in 2025 increased by 4% over 2024 levels.
📈By the end of 2025, US imports from the world remained above the pre-Trump 1.0 trade war linear trend.
📉US imports from China fell by 28% in 2025.
📈US imports from the rest of the world increased by 9%.
🇨🇳China’s share of US imports fell from nearly 22% in the 12 months before June 2018 to only 9% in 2025.
Other economies significantly increased their shares of US imports...
🇹🇼Taiwan by 4.1 percentage points
🇻🇳Vietnam by 3.7 points
🇲🇽Mexico by 2.3 points

💡The US imports from China hit hardest in Trump’s second trade war were those that were omitted from his first.
📈At the beginning of 2025, imports of products that had been omitted from tariffs during the first Trump administration were greater than they were before the Trump 1.0 trade war.
🗓️A 20% tariff on those goods by March 2025 led to a sharp decline in China's exports to the US.
📉In contrast, US imports of Chinese goods that had been hit with 25% tariffs in 2018–19 had already dropped by roughly 40% by the January 2025 inauguration.
